title: A cold pack reads only its cited sources' anchor and fetch-state rows for the freshness stamp, so its time is back near the 56 ms before the stamp
goal: a cold rag.py pack reads only the anchor and fetch-state rows of the sources it cites, not every row of each root's _anchors.csv and _fetch_state.csv; the stamp and the marks it prints stay the same and rag.py eval keeps every row; the median of five cold packs on the darwin host is under 80 ms (117 ms at origin/main 0ae6d30bc on 2026-10-12, 56 ms before ST-ebn65qen)

run: import subprocess,sys,re;o=subprocess.run([sys.executable,'-m','cProfile','-s','ncalls','_tools/rag.py','pack','Claude Code UserPromptSubmit hook timeout'],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout;m=re.search(r'^ *([0-9]+) .*csv.py:[0-9]+[(]__next__[)]',o,re.M);sys.exit(0 if o.startswith('coverage:') and (m is None or int(m.group(1))<6000) else 1)

import subprocess,sys,time,statistics;t=[];exec('for _ in range(5):\n a=time.perf_counter();subprocess.run([sys.executable,\'_tools/rag.py\',\'pack\',\'Claude Code UserPromptSubmit hook timeout\'],capture_output=True);t.append(time.perf_counter()-a)');sys.exit(0 if statistics.median(t)<0.080 else 1)
